note: Salesforce Mapping UI is the admin interface (routes, list builders, forms) for managing salesforce_mapping config entities and salesforce_mapped_object records. It has no config/plugins/Drush of its own; access is gated by the salesforce_mapping permissions (administer salesforce mapping, view salesforce mapping, administer salesforce mapped objects). Medium/hard cases are grounded in real, local, verifiable state: user.role config (which role can administer/view mappings) and the salesforce_mapping config entity the UI creates - verified by pure reads. Namespaced sfmu_* roles/mappings are removed on cleanup.

evals.prompt: Where in the Drupal admin do I manage Salesforce mappings with the Salesforce Mapping UI module, and which permission is required?
evals.expected_output: The mappings list is at /admin/structure/salesforce/mappings (route entity.salesforce_mapping.list), with add/edit/fields/enable/disable/delete forms; it requires the 'administer salesforce mapping' permission. Mapped objects are at /admin/content/salesforce.

evals.prompt: How do I build the individual field mappings for a Salesforce mapping in the UI?
evals.expected_output: Use the field-mapping form at /admin/structure/salesforce/mappings/manage/{mapping}/fields: each row selects a SalesforceMappingField plugin (properties, record_type, ...), a Drupal field/property, a Salesforce field, and a direction. This builds the mapping's field_mappings.

evals.prompt: Does the Salesforce Mapping UI module store its own configuration, or does it manage another module's entities?
evals.expected_output: It has no config of its own - it is the UI layer that manages the salesforce_mapping config entities (and salesforce_mapped_object records) defined by the salesforce_mapping module.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, one role has been granted access to manage Salesforce mappings via the UI. Inspect the roles and name the role that can administer Salesforce mappings.
evals.expected_output: The role is sfmu_known: user.role.sfmu_known includes the 'administer salesforce mapping' permission.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site the role sfmu_view has a single Salesforce mapping related permission. Inspect its configuration and state which permission it has.
evals.expected_output: It has 'view salesforce mapping': user.role.sfmu_view grants the view-mappings permission (read-only access to mapping config).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a role sfmu_task that cannot manage Salesforce mappings. Grant it permission to administer Salesforce mappings (so it can use the mapping UI). Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: The role sfmu_task is granted 'administer salesforce mapping' (user.role.sfmu_task permissions include it).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, set up a new Salesforce mapping named sfmu_map that connects Drupal users to Salesforce Contacts, the kind of thing you would create in the Salesforce mappings screen. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: A salesforce_mapping config entity sfmu_map exists (created via the mapping UI add form at /admin/structure/salesforce/mappings/add or the salesforce_mapping storage), mapping the Drupal user entity to the Salesforce Contact object.
